title: Open-source, Accessible, and Customizable 3D-printed Humanoid Robot Platform | EECS at UC Berkeley
content: Open-source, Accessible, and Customizable 3D-printed Humanoid Robot Platform | EECS at UC Berkeley Open-source, Accessible, and Customizable 3D-printed Humanoid Robot Platform Yufeng Chi EECS Department, University of California, Berkeley Technical Report No. UCB/EECS-2025-207 December 18, 2025 http://www2.eecs.berkeley.edu/Pubs/TechRpts/2025/EECS-2025-207.pdf Despite rapid progress in humanoid robotics, most commercially available platforms remain pricy, closed-source, and inaccessible to the broader community, hindering transparency, customization, and collective innovation. To address this gap, we present Berkeley Humanoid Lite, an open-source humanoid robot designed for affordability, modularity, and ease of replication. The robot employs modular 3D-printed gearboxes and structural components combined with off-the-shelf parts for actuators and electronics. All components can be sourced from common e-commerce platforms and fabricated on standard desktop 3D printers, keeping the total hardware cost under $5,000 (U.S. market). This thesis presents the design considerations when designing and building the robot, and presents results from extensive testing that validates the durability of the printed actuators and alleviates concerns about the reliability of plastic components. The platformâs overall capability is also demonstrated through reinforcement-learning-based locomotion and teleoperated manipulation experiments. All hardware designs, embedded code, and training and deployment frameworks are fully open-sourced. In addition, we provide detailed documentation, tutorials, and community groups to help users get started. Through these efforts, we aim for Berkeley Humanoid Lite to serve as a pivotal step toward democratizing humanoid robotics development. All resources are available at https://lite.berkeley-humanoid.org.
